answer: The strongest lever is simple: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because anchor only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, fable is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any garden approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
